source.description: Project card parser/read point: idprime_get_token_name reads attacker-controlled token-name metadata through iso_ops->read_binary; buf[1] becomes the token-name length.

sink.description: Cleanup frees tokeninfo->label a second time after idprime_get_token_name left it pointing to the already-freed token-name buffer.

root_cause.description: On token-name read failure, idprime_get_token_name frees *tname but leaves the caller-visible tokeninfo->label pointer referring to the freed allocation.

taint_source.description: Unscored fuzz boundary: attacker-controlled PoC bytes are served to OpenSC card operations by the synthetic reader.

tainted_value_origin.description: The second byte read from the synthetic card response controls the allocation size for the token name.

coarse_trace.summary: Reads attacker-controlled token-name length and bytes via the card read abstraction.
Allocates *tname, then frees it on read failure without clearing or delaying the caller-visible pointer assignment.
Card cleanup later frees tokeninfo while tokeninfo->label still aliases the stale *tname allocation.
Frees tokeninfo->label again, triggering the observed double-free.

root_cause_analysis.summary: idprime_get_token_name reads an attacker-controlled token-name length and body through the card reader abstraction. It stores the allocation directly in the caller-visible *tname/tokeninfo->label slot, then frees *tname on a failed body read without clearing that slot. Later tokeninfo cleanup frees tokeninfo->label again, producing the double-free.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch allocates into a local name variable, reads into that local buffer, frees only the local buffer on failure, and assigns *tname = name only after the read succeeds. This prevents tokeninfo->label from ever observing a freed buffer, so the later cleanup cannot double-free it.
